source.title: Catastrophic Fisher Explosion: Early Phase Fisher Matrix Impacts Generalization
source.authors: Stanislaw Jastrzebski; Devansh Arpit; Oliver Åstrand; Giancarlo Kerg; Huan Wang; Caiming Xiong; R. Socher; Kyunghyun Cho; Krzysztof J. Geras

record.file_problem: none; the supplied text includes the paper and appendix.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies batch size and reports test accuracy, and tests whether Fisher Penalty changes the resulting generalization gap. It does not test the other claim versions.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the reported large-batch comparison and Fisher Penalty result. Early Tr(F) correlations, noisy-label experiments, and curvature findings concern related properties or settings not represented by a claim version, so they are listed under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study directly varies batch size and measures held-out accuracy under fixed epoch budgets, and tests Fisher Penalty as an adaptation that recovers large-batch performance. These results test V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase correctly summarizes Appendix E but is narrower than the paper's conclusion. The authors argue that SGD's learning-rate and batch-size regularization effects involve suppressing early Fisher trace; explicit Fisher Penalty can improve generalization and reduce noisy-label memorization. They present large-batch recovery as preliminary evidence.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes and evaluates an explicit Fisher trace penalty, alongside batch-size variation; it does not reproduce the recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported batch-size comparison and Fisher Penalty outcome are specific to SimpleCNN on CIFAR-10 without augmentation; the text reports a 10x larger batch comparison and uses a 2x lower learning rate for the Fisher Penalty experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: Early Fisher trace correlates with final test accuracy, and Fisher Penalty improves performance across several learning-rate settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early Fisher trace predicts held-out performance in the tested vision settings, and explicitly penalizing it can improve performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Fisher Penalty slows learning of synthetic noisy labels more than clean labels and improves test accuracy with partially corrupted training labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fisher Penalty reduces memorization of synthetic label noise in the tested CIFAR-100 models.

fits_no_version.finding: Lower early Fisher trace biases subsequent training toward lower Hessian trace.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early curvature regularization influences final unnormalized curvature in the tested convolutional networks.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2021, PMLR 139)
record.problems: The direct large-batch accuracy comparison in Appendix E is internally inconsistent: it says the larger batch lowers accuracy by 3.24% but lists 76.94% compared with 73.7%. Authors describe large-batch evidence as preliminary. The paper uses vision tasks only and notes that its Fisher Penalty approximates Tr(F) with minibatch gradients.
record.rows_left_out: No additional V5 rows with unambiguous numeric results are given for the direct batch-size comparison. Other Fisher Penalty results vary learning rate or regularizer rather than batch size and do not directly test V5. No rows omitted for the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: No matched comparison of fitting fully random labels and generalizing on natural labels, including chance-level held-out accuracy under random labels.
No width sweep beyond the width required for zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.

Language models, systematic estimation of workload-dependent batch-size thresholds, longer-training remedies, learning-rate scaling with warmup, and normalization changes are untested. Fixed epoch budgets are tested.
No magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation measure, ranking against norm and margin measures, or direct test of that measure against generalization gaps.
No removal and retraining comparison between highly memorized examples and random examples.

missing.what: Direct fixed-budget batch-size comparison: batch sizes 520, 500 and 480 yield maximum test accuracies 90.72%, 90.78% and 90.76%; batch sizes 120, 100 and 80 yield 95.52%, 94.38% and 94.84%. Learning rate is 0.02, training lasts 250 epochs, and results average across 32 seeds. Record these held-out results separately from the curvature measures.

Additional batch-size sweeps use ResNet-26 on CIFAR-10 with augmentation at batch sizes 100, 500 and 700, and CIFAR-100 without augmentation at 100, 300 and 700. Both use 200 epochs and learning rate 0.02, with 32 seeds per setting. Figure 7 reports maximum test accuracy and variability; Figure 9 reports near-ceiling training accuracy. The supplied text does not preserve individual plotted test values or their batch-size assignments, so numerical ordering cannot be reconstructed from it.
missing.locator: Section 3; Appendix A.1, Figures 7 and 9; Appendix I.1

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for any listed version. Table 1 resolves R1's accuracy ordering. Fisher Penalty recovery supports an adaptation already allowed by V5, so it does not by itself warrant limits_scope. Fisher and Hessian traces do not measure the magnitude-aware sharpness specified in V7.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare fitting random labels with generalization on natural labels.
No network-width sweep or interpolation-threshold test.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
Tests SimpleCNN on CIFAR-10 without augmentation; does not test language models, other image classifiers, fixed epoch budgets, or the cited adaptive recipe changes.
Measures Tr(F), not magnitude-scaled weight perturbation sharpness or comparisons against norm- and margin-based measures.
Does not remove selected memorized examples and retrain.

rows.subject: SimpleCNN
rows.operation_detail: Compared test accuracy after training with a 10x larger batch size at the same learning rate.
rows.note: The text says the larger batch has 3.24% lower test accuracy, but gives the values as 76.94% compared with 73.7%, which implies the opposite direction. Values are retained as written.
rows.check: The claimed inconsistency is resolved by Table 1: 76.94% is the reference small-batch accuracy and 73.7% is the large-batch accuracy, a decline of 3.24 percentage points. Appendix E uses the Table 1 recipe with batch size increased from 128 to 1280; Appendix I.2 specifies 300 epochs. The architecture also has its final fully connected layer reduced to 128 units.

rows.subject: SimpleCNN
rows.operation_detail: Applied Fisher Penalty during training with a large batch size.

conditions.value: 2x lower; training with this learning rate alone reaches 73.59% test accuracy

rows.note: The text says Fisher Penalty improves test accuracy from 73.59% to 78.7% and reduces peak Tr(F).
rows.check: The accuracy values are correct. Specify a 300-epoch budget and batch size 1280. Fisher Penalty is applied every optimization step using the first 128 examples. The 73.59% comparator already uses the same halved learning rate, so the improvement to 78.7% isolates adding the penalty at that learning rate.

relationships.condition: SimpleCNN on CIFAR-10 without augmentation, unchanged learning rate, batch size increased from 128 to 1280 under the 300-epoch recipe
relationships.reason: R1 reports accuracy falling from 76.94% to 73.7%, supporting a large-batch penalty under a fixed epoch budget.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy was lower after batch size increased with an unchanged learning rate, but this comparison remains unverified.

relationships.condition: Large-batch SimpleCNN on CIFAR-10 without augmentation, Fisher Penalty added at a halved learning rate
relationships.reason: R2 improves accuracy from 73.59% to 78.7%, supporting V5's allowance that regularization changes can remove the penalty.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy improved after Fisher Penalty was added at a reduced learning rate, but this comparison remains unverified.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10 with augmentation, fixed learning rate 0.02 and 250 training epochs, batch sizes 480–520 versus 80–120
relationships.reason: Appendix A.4, Figure 14 reports maximum test accuracies of 90.72–90.78% for larger batches versus 94.38–95.52% for smaller batches; this verdict uses text omitted from the rows.
relationships.display_finding: Maximum test accuracy was lower with larger batches under augmentation, but these comparisons remain unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: SimpleCNN on CIFAR-10 without augmentation, large batch with Fisher Penalty
reader_labels.reason: Fisher Penalty improves test accuracy from the stated 73.59% baseline to 78.7%, showing the gap can be reduced by an added regularizer (R2). The direct large-batch comparison has internally inconsistent direction and values (R1).
